policy.title: Benchmark evidence policy
policy.summary: Benchmarks are supporting evidence, not our final ranking. We identify the exact model/version, source, snapshot date and harness. Product scores are not treated as model scores, and results from different harness versions are not compared directly.

sources.name: Arena Text Leaderboard
sources.measures: Human preference in anonymous model-vs-model battles across open-ended text tasks.
sources.caveat: A product such as ChatGPT or Claude can change its default model; Arena ranks specific model versions, not the whole product. Checked 2026-09-14 and re-checked 2026-09-21, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-19: /leaderboard/text 308-redirects to /leaderboard/chat/text, which now answers a Cloudflare challenge to plain HTTP clients, so this check read the board in a headless Chromium session and cross-read the rendered rows against the page's own embedded per-model JSON (rank, rating, vote count and modelKey for all 416 listings). The board served a new snapshot dated 2026-10-15 (vote cutoff 2026-10-15T13:00:00.000Z, 8,834,211 votes, 416 models), replacing the 2026-10-08 snapshot (8,734,330 votes, 414 models). Every tracked row was re-read from it and all six keep the same exact model key as before. All six ranks fell by one to three places, five ratings were unchanged to the board's integer rounding and Gemini lost one point (1446 to 1445), and every tracked vote count fell by 13 to 63 votes even though the board-wide total rose by 99,881 - the pattern produced by re-filtering existing battles, not by a change in product quality. Two newer same-board listings were again seen and deliberately NOT added as rows: grok-4.5-text (rank 52 in this snapshot, 1466 +/-4, 39,896 votes) and deepseek-v4-pro-high-20260813 (rank 56, 1465 +/-7, 9,800 votes). This registry carries one representative exact listing per product family, and the site's generators key rows by tool_slug, so a second row for the same family would silently overwrite the first in every generated comparison rather than adding evidence.

sources.name: Arena-Rank methodology
sources.measures: Bradley-Terry ratings with reweighting and confidence intervals from pairwise preference data.
sources.use_for: Explaining how Arena scores are produced
sources.caveat: Human preference can reward style and verbosity; it is not an objective factuality test.

sources.name: SWE-bench Verified
sources.measures: Percentage of 500 human-validated real GitHub issues resolved by a coding model or agent.
sources.caveat: Scores depend heavily on the agent harness. mini-SWE-agent v1.x and v2.x results are not directly comparable. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-19: the site still publishes a machine-readable results payload (an embedded leaderboard-data JSON block covering Multilingual, Test, Verified, Lite and Multimodal). The Verified group is unchanged at 180 rows dated 2023-10-10 to 2026-02-26; the newest is still a mini-SWE-agent 2.0.0 run on Gemini 3 Pro at 69.6% resolved, and the highest score in the group is Sonar Foundation Agent + Claude 4.5 Opus at 79.2% (2025-12-05), tied by live-SWE-agent + Claude 4.5 Opus medium at 79.2% (2025-12-15). No Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Replit, or other tracked end-user product appears in that Verified set, so no product-level coding row is added from it. The page text still confirms the 500-instance human-validated subset.

sources.name: LiveBench
sources.measures: Objective, frequently refreshed tasks across reasoning, math, coding, language, instruction following and data analysis.
sources.caveat: Always state the release; questions and model configurations change between snapshots. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-19: the repository is live and active (latest commit seen 2026-10-18, adding a deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-max configuration), but its own changelog.md still ends at 2026-01-08 and the README still shows "Top models as of 30th September 2024". The material change is on the website: livebench.ai is now branded "LiveBench 2.0 - a challenging, contamination-free long-horizon AI benchmark", and its bundled release list carries two generations - v1 releases from 2024-06-24 through 2026-06-25, plus a 2.0 release dated 2026-10-14 served at /data/20261014/table.csv with 48 model rows across 7 categories (long_agentic, reasoning, coding, browser, data_analysis, research, design). The v1 June table at /v1/table_2026_06_25.csv still holds 71 model rows across 23 task columns and was re-uploaded with HTTP Last-Modified 2026-10-18. The two generations use different task sets and must never be pooled or compared, and neither is a product-level ranking: treat LiveBench as release-pinned model evidence only.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis methodology
sources.measures: Independent intelligence, latency, speed, price, speech, image and video model evaluations.
sources.use_for: Cost/speed context and non-text modality methodology
sources.caveat: API model measurements do not equal the complete end-user product experience. Re-checked 2026-10-19: the methodology page is live and still serves no dated per-model score table, so no Artificial Analysis row exists in this registry.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard (frozen; subdomain now serves 4.0)
sources.measures: Accuracy of an agent + model + reasoning-effort configuration on 89 complex containerized terminal tasks.
sources.use_for: Coding agents and terminal-capable development tools
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-19: https://www.tbench.ai/leaderboard/terminal-bench/2.1 still returns a 308 redirect to https://www.tbench.ai/?version=2.1, and every route on that host still serves the Terminal-Bench 4.0 board (title "Terminal-Bench 4.0", leaderboard slug "4-0-0", board updated_at 2026-10-06T23:20:25Z, still 35 rows at 330 trials each). No 2.1 rows can be read from this URL on any date, and no archived 2.1 board exists on the site. The 4.0 board lists only Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Muse Code and mini-SWE-agent configurations and carries no Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf or Replit entry, so nothing here can move the registry's coding row. Never present this as a model-only score; keep agent, exact model, effort, trial count and integrity metadata visible.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Image methodology
sources.measures: Blind pairwise image preference with exact model/version and matched prompt conditions.
sources.caveat: Keep text-to-image and editing pools separate; old model versions are historical evidence only. Re-checked 2026-10-19: the page is live with separate text-to-image and editing sections and still serves no dated score table.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Video methodology
sources.measures: Modality-separated video quality, latency and price comparisons.
sources.caveat: Do not compare Elo across different video modalities or output settings. Re-checked 2026-10-19: the methodology page is live and states that each modality has its own Elo pool in the Video Arena, so silent and audio-enabled outputs are not compared directly and editing is not compared with generation. No dated score table is served.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis TTS methodology
sources.measures: Provider-voice and controlled-voice human-preference comparisons for text-to-speech.
sources.caveat: Controlled-voice and provider-voice arenas answer different questions and must remain separate. Re-checked 2026-10-19: the canonical page is live at https://artificialanalysis.ai/text-to-speech/methodology and it separates the provider-voice and controlled-voice sections. No dated score table is served.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench: Cursor CLI + Grok 4.5 submission
sources.measures: Maintainer-verified Terminal-Bench 2.1 submission record for one exact Cursor CLI configuration.
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21, re-hashed 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-19 against the raw submission file (sha256 a73454861c91299b501637e6df6082f2f16cf9c9f6c98f07bce315189f82eb23, 29,033 bytes, byte-identical on every check): Cursor CLI 2026.07.08-0c04a8a + cursor/grok-4.5 at high effort, 79.33% +/- 1.46, 445 trials, 8.99% reward-hack disqualifications, dated 2026-07-09. Two limits sit on it: the Terminal-Bench 2.1 README states "Community submissions are currently closed for Terminal-Bench 2.1", so the 2.1 board is frozen, and the live 4.0 board carries no Cursor entry, so there is no current Cursor reading to compare it to. Scores from 2.1 and 4.0 are different harness versions and must never be compared with each other.

sources.name: Harbor Hub — Terminal-Bench 2.1 dataset
sources.measures: The live dataset record for Terminal-Bench 2.1: which tasks the frozen board ran and which version is published.
sources.use_for: Confirming the task set behind a Terminal-Bench 2.1 configuration score
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-19: the dataset page describes "Version 2.1 of Terminal-Bench", and the Terminal-Bench 2.1 repository independently holds 89 task directories (91 entries minus the README and dataset.toml files), matching the 89 tasks this page reports. Terminal-Bench 4.0 is not a "larger" task set: the current Terminal-Bench repository holds 66 task directories at its v4.0.0 release tag (published 2026-08-26). 2.1 and 4.0 are different task sets, not a small/large pair. The Hub's latest published revision is still 2.0.2 (revision 6). This page publishes the task list, not leaderboard scores; it cannot upgrade a 2.1 score into a 4.0 score.

snapshot_summary: Arena Text published a new snapshot dated 15 Oct 2026 (vote cutoff 2026-10-15T13:00:00Z, 8,834,211 votes across 416 models), replacing the 8 Oct 2026 snapshot this file previously pinned (8,734,330 votes across 414 models). All six tracked listings were re-read from it and all six keep the same exact model key as before. Every rank fell by one to three places, five of the six ratings were unchanged to the board's integer rounding and Gemini dropped one point, and every tracked vote count fell by 13 to 63 votes even though the board-wide total rose by ~100,000. That is the shape of battle re-filtering, not evidence that any product changed quality, and every move sits inside a +/-2 to +/-6 confidence interval.
